title: Fixation of carbon dioxide by macrocyclic lanthanide(III) complexes under neutral conditions producing self-assembled trimeric carbonato-bridged compounds with μ3-η2:η2:η2 bonding

material_class.structural_family: μ3-η2:η2:η2 carbonato-bridged trinuclear tetraiminodiphenolate macrocycle complex

synthesis.procedure: All complexes 1–7 were prepared analogously. Finely ground [{Pb(LH2)(ClO4)}6](ClO4)6 (0.486 g, 0.1 mmol) was dissolved in boiling acetonitrile (50 mL). A methanol solution (10 mL) of freshly prepared LnCl3·nH2O (0.6 mmol; Ln = La for 1) was added. The mixture was stirred and refluxed for 2 h. Precipitated PbCl2 was removed by filtration and the filtrate was rotary-evaporated to dryness. The residue was extracted with hot methanol (2 × 20 mL) and the combined filtrate was treated with water (2 mL). The yellow 95:5 methanol–water solution was kept in air at room temperature for several hours, depositing orange-yellow crystals of the carbonato-bridged product formed by atmospheric CO2 fixation. The product was collected by filtration and washed with cold methanol and diethyl ether.
synthesis.temperature: reflux in acetonitrile–methanol for 2 h, then room temperature crystallization in air
synthesis.time: reflux 2 h; crystallization for several hours
synthesis.vessel_or_method: stirring/reflux followed by rotary evaporation and air crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filter off PbCl2; evaporate to dryness; extract with hot methanol (2 × 20 mL); add water (2 mL); crystallize in air; filter and wash with cold methanol and diethyl ether

properties.summary: No luminescence in acetonitrile at 298 K. In an acetonitrile–toluene glassy matrix at 77 K, Sm(III) shows four 4G5/2 → 6HJ emission bands; the strongest is 4G5/2 → 6H7/2. Ligand LH2 acts as a sensitizer; overall luminescence intensity order is Eu3+ > Sm3+ > Tb3+.

properties.summary: Weak Eu(III) luminescence in acetonitrile at 298 K. At 77 K in acetonitrile–toluene glass, five 5D0 → 7FJ bands are resolved; the 5D0 → 7F0 band at 576 nm indicates low site symmetry. Integrated 5D0 → 7F2 / 5D0 → 7F1 intensity ratio is about 3.3. Ligand LH2 sensitizes Eu(III); intensity order Eu3+ > Sm3+ > Tb3+.

properties.summary: Powdered 5 shows very weak antiferromagnetic exchange among three S = 7/2 Gd(III) ions through the μ3-carbonate bridge (nearly equilateral triangle, average Gd···Gd 4.99 Å). χMT at 300 K is slightly below the spin-only value for three uncoupled Gd3+ ions and falls sharply below 12 K. Fit of the equilateral-triangle Hamiltonian gives J = −0.042 cm−1 and g = 1.96. At 77 K, excitation at 400 nm produces ligand-centered emission at about 465 nm (21500 cm−1) assigned to the LH2 triplet, used as a reference for sensitization of Sm/Eu/Tb.

properties.summary: No luminescence in solution at 298 K. At 77 K the Tb(III) complex is weakly luminescent except for a moderate 5D4 → 7F5 band at 540 nm; 5D4 → 7F6 overlaps ligand emission at 465 nm. Inefficient sensitization is attributed to a small energy gap ΔE(3ππ* − 5D4) of 1000 cm−1 versus the >1850 cm−1 optimum.

synthesis.procedure: Obtained analogously to 1–7 using [{Pb(LH2)(ClO4)}6](ClO4)6 (0.1 mmol) and YCl3·nH2O (0.6 mmol). Transmetallation in boiling acetonitrile/methanol, removal of PbCl2, methanol–water workup, and air crystallization afforded the dinuclear μ2-carbonato product rather than a trinuclear μ3-carbonato analogue.
